kaps_punt: Verskillende ekostelsels: 'n ekostelsel is 'n gebied waar lewende en nie-lewende dinge afhanklik is van mekaar op verskillende maniere; daar is baie verskillende ekostelsels, soos riviere, berge, see, rotsagtige kus, damme, vleilande, grasvelde, woude en woestyne, wat verskillende soorte lewende dinge onderhou. Lewende en nie-lewende dinge in ekostelsels: in 'n ekostelsel is daar sekere verhoudings tussen lewende dinge (plante, diere/mense, mikro-organismes), en nie-lewende dinge (lug, water, sonlig, grond) in 'n bepaalde gebied *. [Voetnoot *: Gesonde ekostelsels is afhanklik van voldoende biodiversiteit van plante, diere en hul habitatte.]

items.bewering: Paddas skuil tussen die riete en vang die insekte wat daar rondvlieg.
items.bron: Britannica, 'What Do Frogs Eat?' (britannica.com/science/What-Do-Frogs-Eat): adult frogs are primarily insectivores; SANBI Animal of the Week, Pickersgill's reed frog, and SANBI PlantZAfrica Phragmites australis: reed beds give shelter to frogs and other animals.

items.bewering: Die riete self het modder, water en sonlig nodig om te groei.
items.bron: SANBI PlantZAfrica, Phragmites australis (pza.sanbi.org/phragmites-australis): an aquatic or semi-aquatic plant of wetlands and wet soils; National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis': plants need sunlight and water.

items.bewering: So hang die lewende dinge van mekaar en van die nie-lewende dinge om hulle af. Die hele gebied met al sy lewende en nie-lewende dele saam noem ons 'n ekostelsel.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Biomes, Ecosystems, and Habitats': an ecosystem is the living community together with the non-living world in one area, and the interactions between them.

items.bewering: Die son en die lug het egter nie die paddas of die riete nodig nie.
items.bron: True as worded: the sun and the air do not depend on one dam's frogs and reeds. National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis', says the oxygen in the air comes from plants and algae across the whole world, and the lesson says the same two blocks later ('Groen plante gee ... suurstof aan die lug af'). So the sentence holds only for these particular frogs and reeds. As a general rule ('non-living things never need living things') it would be false. For a person to note, not a correction.

items.bewering: 'n Habitat is net die plek waar een plant of dier lewe. 'n Ekostelsel is die hele gebied met al daardie plekke daarin.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Habitat': the place where an organism makes its home; Forest Preserve District of Will County, 'Habitat vs. ecosystem': a habitat is a location, while an ecosystem is the whole area with the interactions of its living and non-living parts.

items.bewering: Daar is baie verskillende ekostelsels op aarde. Party is nat en ander is baie droog. Elkeen het daarom sy eie soorte plante en diere wat daar goed lewe.
items.bron: CBD Article 2 / UNESCO glossary: ecosystem diversity includes deserts, forests, wetlands, mountains, lakes and rivers; SANBI Grassland Biome and wetland classification pages describe distinct communities in each.

items.bewering: Rivier: vars water wat stroomaf vloei. Visse soos die geelvis swem daarin.
items.bron: SANBI species assessment, Labeobarbus aeneus (speciesstatus.sanbi.org/assessment/last-assessment/89/); Wikipedia 'Smallmouth yellowfish': a freshwater fish of the Orange-Vaal river system that prefers clear, flowing water in large rivers.

items.bewering: Berg: hoë, steil hange met baie rotse. Klipspringers spring daar van rots tot rots.
items.bron: Animal Diversity Web, Oreotragus oreotragus: found only in rocky habitat, including rocky hills, koppies, gorges and mountains up to 4 000 m, and adapted to jump from rock to rock; San Diego Zoo, Klipspringer.

items.bewering: See: 'n baie groot gebied soutwater. Dolfyne en haaie swem daarin.
items.bron: Marine Protected Areas South Africa, 'Iconic species' (marineprotectedareas.org.za/iconic-species); PMC7549814 (Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins off the South African south coast); over 100 shark species recorded in South African waters.

items.bewering: Rotsagtige kus: rotse waaroor die golwe breek. Klipmossels sit styf aan die rotse vas.
items.bron: Afrikaans Wikipedia, Skerppuntklipmossel, and the Afrikaans-English dictionaries at translate.com and majstro.com: 'klipmossel' is the Afrikaans word for a limpet, not a mussel. Phys.org, 'Limpet sticking power down to mucus, not muscle' (2020), and Beachcomber Guide, 'The amazing limpets of South Africa': limpets hold firmly to rocks against wave action. The claim is true for limpets. It would also be true for mussels, which attach with threads, so it holds under either reading.

items.bewering: Dam: water wat stil in 'n kom of agter 'n wal staan. Baie paddas lê hulle eiers daarin.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'African bullfrog' and Kromme Enviro Trust, 'Frogs of the greater St Francis area': many South African frogs lay their eggs in shallow pools and ponds; some species lay above the water or in foam nests. 'Baie' is correctly narrower than 'alle'.

items.bewering: Vleiland: grond wat lank nat is of onder vlak water lê. Riete groei daar dig op mekaar.
items.bron: National Water Act definition as quoted by SANBI (Biodiversity Series 22, wetland classification): land where the water table is usually at or near the surface, or which is periodically covered with shallow water, supporting vegetation adapted to saturated soil; SANBI PlantZAfrica: Phragmites forms dense reed beds in wetlands.

items.bewering: Grasveld: oop land met baie gras en min of geen bome. Blesbokke wei daar.
items.bron: SANBI PlantZAfrica, Grassland Biome (pza.sanbi.org/vegetation/grassland-biome): dominated by grasses, trees absent except in local habitats; Wikipedia 'Blesbok': a grazer of open Highveld grassland, endemic to South Africa.

items.bewering: Woud: hoë bome wat naby mekaar groei, met skaduwee onder hulle. Die Knysnaloerie lewe hoog in die bome.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Southern Afrotemperate Forest' (tall, shady, multilayered forest); Botanical Society of South Africa, 'Forests of South Africa' (tree crowns overlap to form a canopy with shade-loving plants beneath); Birds of the World, Knysna Turaco: lives in evergreen forest and forages mainly in the tree canopy.

items.bewering: Woestyn: 'n plek waar baie min reën val, met sand of klippe. Die gemsbok kan lank sonder drinkwater klaarkom.
items.bron: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, 'What Is a Desert?': deserts are defined by aridity, and only about a quarter of desert area is sand, the rest rock and gravel, so 'sand of klippe' is right; Wikipedia 'Gemsbok' and krugerpark.co.za: can go months without surface water, getting moisture from food.

items.bewering: Die lewende dele van 'n ekostelsel is die plante, die diere en die mikro-organismes. Mense is ook diere, en ons is deel van die ekostelsels waar ons woon.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Human' and Animal Diversity Web, Animalia: humans belong to kingdom Animalia; National Geographic Education, 'Biomes, Ecosystems, and Habitats' (the biotic community).

items.bewering: Mikro-organismes is so klein dat jy hulle net deur 'n mikroskoop kan sien. Hulle lewe in die grond, in die water en selfs op jou vel.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'microorganisms': organisms too small to see with the unaided eye, seen only through a microscope, found in soil, water, air and on living things; NHGRI (genome.gov), 'NIH researchers find thousands of new microorganisms living on human skin'.

items.bewering: Die meeste van hierdie klein lewende dinge maak niemand siek nie.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'microorganisms': most microorganisms are essential to life, and only some cause disease; Wikipedia 'Pathogen': only a small fraction of bacterial species are pathogenic to humans.

items.bewering: Die lug hou die suurstof wat die meeste lewende dinge vir asemhaling gebruik.
items.bron: Could not settle. The lesson counts micro-organisms among living things, and by number micro-organisms are almost all living things. Many bacteria and archaea are anaerobic (OpenStax Biology 2e, 'Prokaryotic Metabolism'; ScienceDirect Topics, 'Anaerobe'). Published estimates of how much of Earth's microbial life lives in oxygen-free places (sediments, the deep subsurface) disagree: Magnabosco et al. 2018 (Nature Geoscience) and Flemming & Wuertz 2019 (Nature Reviews Microbiology) give quite different pictures. So 'most living things use oxygen' is true of plants and animals but cannot be defended once microbes are counted. The same claim is in the 'suurstof' begrip. A safe narrowing is 'die meeste plante en diere', which keeps the subject and narrows the quantifier. A person should decide.

items.bewering: Plante neem ook 'n ander gas uit die lug om hulle kos te maak.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis': plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and use sunlight and water to make sugar.

items.bewering: Elke plant en dier het water nodig, en baie van hulle lewe self daarin.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'living things': plants and animals need water to survive and grow; aquatic habitats confirmed via the SANBI wetland and river sources above.

items.bewering: Sonlig gee plante die energie om kos te maak en verwarm die land en die water.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis' (light energy drives photosynthesis) and 'The Power of the Sun' (solar radiation heats Earth's land and water).

items.bewering: Die grond hou plante se wortels vas en gee hulle water en voedingstowwe. Erdwurms en miere maak ook hulle huise in die grond.
items.bron: FAO, 'Soil health' (fao.org/4/i0211e/i0211e02.pdf) and the FAO Soil Macrofauna Field Manual: soil gives roots physical support, water and nutrients, and earthworms, termites and ants are its main macrofauna.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge gebruik die nie-lewende dele en verander dit ook. Groen plante gee byvoorbeeld suurstof aan die lug af wanneer hulle kos maak. Baie diere asem daardie suurstof dan weer in.
items.blok: Lewende dinge verander die nie-lewende dele
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis': plants release oxygen into the air as they make food, and the oxygen we breathe comes from photosynthesis.

items.bewering: In graad 5 het jy geleer wat biodiversiteit is.
items.bron: Could not confirm from a usable source. A search summary of the DBE CAPS document gives Grade 5 Term 1 as 'many different plants and animals living in different habitats on Earth' and does not show the word 'biodiversity'. Every result that did link the term to Grade 5 was a textbook, a teacher guide or a commercial worksheet (Siyavula/Thunderbolt Kids, a DBE learner book, Teacha!, Twinkl), and those were not used. I could not get readable text from the official CAPS PDF. A person can settle this at once by checking whether our own Grade 5 lessons define 'biodiversiteit'. If they do not, the sentence should not say the learner learnt it.

items.bewering: 'n Gesonde ekostelsel het genoeg daarvan nodig. Baie soorte plante gee aan die diere baie soorte kos en skuiling.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Habitat' (food and shelter are core habitat needs); ResearchGate/Oikos, 'Plant species loss decreases arthropod diversity and shifts trophic structure'.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n grasveld wat sy veldblomme en baie van sy grassoorte verloor. Party insekte en voëls kry dan nie meer genoeg kos nie, en hulle kan ook verdwyn. Die diere wat daardie insekte en voëls eet, kry dan swaar.
items.bron: 'Plant species loss decreases arthropod diversity and shifts trophic structure' (Ecology Letters); ScienceDirect 2026, 'Insect pollinators profit from moderate diversification of intensively used grasslands': fewer plant species means fewer pollinating insects, and the decline of insects is followed by a decline in insect-eating grassland birds. 'Party' and 'kan' are correctly hedged.

items.bewering: Die plekke waar die plante en diere lewe, moet ook heel bly.
items.bron: Discover Wildlife, 'Habitats and ecosystems: how they affect biodiversity', and the CBD definition, which includes the ecosystems organisms are part of: habitat loss reduces biodiversity.

items.bewering: ekostelsel: 'n Gebied waar lewende dinge van mekaar en van die nie-lewende dinge om hulle afhang.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Biomes, Ecosystems, and Habitats': living and non-living things interacting in one area. Read alone it fits only an ecosystem.

items.bewering: habitat: Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Habitat'; Britannica Kids, 'habitat'.

items.bewering: vleiland: Land wat lank nat is of onder vlak water lê, met plante wat in nat grond groei, soos riete.
items.bron: National Water Act definition as quoted by SANBI (Biodiversity Series 22): water table at or near the surface, or periodically covered by shallow water, with vegetation adapted to saturated soil.

items.bewering: mikro-organisme: 'n Lewende ding wat so klein is dat 'n mens dit net deur 'n mikroskoop kan sien.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'microorganisms'; Dictionary.com, 'microorganism': an organism too small to be seen with the naked eye.

items.bewering: suurstof: 'n Gas wat plante afgee wanneer hulle kos maak, en wat die meeste lewende dinge vir asemhaling gebruik.
items.bron: The first half is confirmed (National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis'). The second half is the same 'die meeste lewende dinge' claim as in 'Die nie-lewende dele' and cannot be settled once micro-organisms are counted as living things (see that item). Whatever ruling is made there must also be made here, so the two do not end up differing.

items.bewering: asemhaling: Om suurstof te gebruik om energie uit jou kos te kry.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Aerobic respiration': organisms combine oxygen with food molecules to release chemical energy. This describes aerobic respiration, which is right for this lesson's plants and animals.

items.bewering: voedingstof: 'n Stof wat 'n lewende ding nodig het om te groei en gesond te bly. Party voedingstowwe in kos gee ook energie.
items.bron: LibreTexts, An Introduction to Nutrition (Zimmerman) 1.3 'What Are Nutrients?', and MedlinePlus nutrition definitions: nutrients are substances the body needs to function; some provide energy (carbohydrates, fats, proteins), others do not (vitamins, minerals).

items.bewering: biodiversiteit: Hoeveel verskillende soorte lewende dinge daar in 'n plek of op die hele Aarde is.
items.bron: CBD Article 2 (via UNESCO World Heritage glossary and PMC3002324, 'Q&A: What is biodiversity?'): the variety of living organisms, at species, genetic and ecosystem level. The begrip gives the species level only, which is an acceptable simplification for Grade 6 and not a false one.

opsomming: Nothing is contradicted, but two claims could not be settled: 'die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof vir asemhaling' (in the study text and the 'suurstof' definition) does not hold once micro-organisms count as living things, which this lesson says they do, and 'die meeste plante en diere' would be safe; and 'In graad 5 het jy geleer wat biodiversiteit is' was confirmed only by textbooks, so someone should check our own Grade 5 lessons.
